question: Under what condition can one whose mind is fixed on that remain uncut even when being cut?
premises: Cutting is being applied to the person in question.
The mind remains fixed upon that object or state.
Such fixation alters the effect of the cutting action.
inference: When the mind is fixed on that, the act of cutting does not sever in the expected way.
uncertainties: The precise referent of tad and tan remains unclear from this verse alone.
plain_english: Even when being cut, one whose mind is fixed on that is not cut, just so.
